image_prompt.text: The alley itself as walkable circulation end to end — asphalt roadway with white markings, a speed bump, and puddles standing on the surface, sized for foot traffic between the storefronts

Continuous modern buildings pressing in on both sides of the alley — a cafe, a boutique, a convenience store, apartments, and glass storefronts — built up as one dense Tokyo/Seoul city block rather than scattered structures
Highly detailed photo spots along the alley — the lit cafe frontage, the bench-and-tree corner, the vending machine row — composed as backdrops for screenshots and roleplay scenes
Aesthetic neon signage stacked up one alley corner, bright enough at night to be read from either end of the street
Warm street lamps, utility poles, hanging signs, benches, small trees, and vending machines lining both sides of the alley
Fire escape stairs and window AC units on the building facades above the storefronts
Decorative cables strung overhead across the alley, bicycles parked against the walls, and stacked delivery boxes by the doorways
A semi-realistic, lived-in night atmosphere — wet asphalt reflecting the neon and lamp glow, grime and wear on the walls

notes: Preset caveat: Morph Roleplay kept with its shape (settlement-static) and vignette-photo and landmark-focal, but social-hub was dropped — a narrow alley contradicts a deliberately oversized gathering square, and building one would add a plaza the prompt did not ask for.

Entertainment (showcase / environment demo) was considered as a second genre and not loaded: the prompt says roleplay twice, and Roleplay's own settlement-static plus vignette-photo already express a fixed, detailed, photo-oriented set, so the second file would have added nothing the dominant genre could not say.
Universal Option used: settlement-density, for the stated request that both sides of the alley be continuous modern buildings rather than scattered structures. No other universal option was applied.
layout_placement is empty because every pick here is an image-side environment feature; nothing requested is an invisible volume, marker, or trigger.
Routed P0: the prompt describes exteriors only — storefronts, facades, fire escapes, AC units — so no interior transition is required. Interiors remain available as an upgrade.

would have asked: Sounds like a fixed, pre-built roleplay set rather than a town you claim property in — one alley you walk down, dense modern buildings on both sides, photo-ready spots at the cafe frontage and the bench corner, and a neon sign stack to orient by, plus the street furniture, facade details, and night look you listed. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: should the cafe, boutique, or convenience store actually be enterable? That is a real cost — interiors get generated separately and the build is slower — and nothing in the prompt says players go inside, so it was built as storefronts you see from the street.

would have asked: the alley reads as walking-only, so it was built as pedestrian circulation rather than a 15-30 stud vehicle street; the asphalt, white markings and speed bump are surface detail. Confirm if cars need to drive down it.
would have asked: 'lived-in' was read as wear and clutter rather than people — do you want ambient NPCs (shopkeepers, passers-by) in the alley?
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?
